description: Bunnymark, the 2D sprite benchmark PixiJS made famous (after Iain Lobb's): bunnies thrown in, falling under gravity, bouncing off the floor and the sides, each one a textured quad of helder.sprite's SpriteBatch, all of them one run of one texture: a single draw call however many there are.

Press and hold (or Space) to add 500 a frame. The overlay shows the bunnies, and the most drawn while the last second's median frame stayed under 17.5 ms: the count at 60 fps. The bunnies' sheet is drawn in code; nothing is allocated a frame. As PixiJS's, the canvas is drawn a pixel a point (on a high-density screen too) and not multisampled: a sprite is 80 bytes of vertices, PixiJS's 96.

compare.note: The library alone (PixiJS 7.4.2's: 0.46 MB, 0.14 gzipped); the bunnies' image and the page's code on top.

credits: After PixiJS's Bunnymark and Iain Lobb's original; the bunnies drawn in code (MIT, helder)
